svg.title: Five diagnostic questions, asked in order, and where each yes leads
svg.desc: A hand-drawn vertical walk. Five numbered questions run down a spine, each with an arrow marked yes leading right to the failure mode it diagnoses and the first thing to look at. A fluent but off-topic answer means distraction; rules present and violated anyway means confusion; a self-contradiction means conflict; quality dropping only on long contexts means lost in the middle; tool calls without progress means tool-storm. The spine continues past the fifth question to a dashed box: none of the five means a model bug or a systems bug, separately diagnosable and not a context bug. A caption notes the same mode wears different clothes in different products.
svg.text: A diagnostic walk: five questions, in order
When a bug report arrives, ask them in this order. The first yes is almost always the right one.
Is the answer fluent but off-topic?
yes
Distraction
look at the retrieved set, then the prompt
Were the rules present, and violated anyway?
yes
Confusion
audit the system prompt and tool descriptions
Does it contradict itself, or an earlier turn?
yes
Conflict
two sources disagree with no precedence rule
Does quality drop only when the context is long?
yes
Lost in the middle
bookend the packing; otherwise compress
Is the trace full of tool calls without progress?
yes
Tool-storm
trim the catalogue, cap the loop
none of the five
A model bug, or a systems bug
separately diagnosable; neither is a context bug
The same mode wears different clothes: in a coding agent, distraction edits the wrong file; in a support agent, it answers a shipping question with a returns policy.
